headline: House resolution that would have impeached Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas was voted down on February 6, 2024.
what_it_does: This resolution would have impeached Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas for high crimes and misdemeanors. The charges included his handling of issues involving fentanyl and border security. Impeachment by the House is a formal charge, not a removal from office. If it had passed, the case would have gone to the Senate for a trial, where a two-thirds vote is needed to remove an official.

who_it_affects.group: Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas
who_it_affects.how: He would have been formally charged by the House and faced a Senate trial that could have removed him from office.
Senators would have been required to hold a trial and vote on whether to convict and remove the Secretary.
